look_here_first: Look for the true scarlet leatherflower: a nodding ovoid-to-urn-shaped flower with thick rose-red to scarlet sepals and sharply recurved tips, but without the expanded crispate margins of C. pitcheri.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: 1-pinnate leaves with 6–10 leaflets plus tendril-like terminal leaflet

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: four thick scarlet sepals with non-expanded non-crispate margins

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial climbing vine to roughly 3 m.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: 1-pinnate; 6–10 leathery leaflets plus a tendril-like terminal leaflet; often glaucous beneath and reticulate.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Axillary scarlet leathery urn; sepal margins not expanded or crispate; tips recurved.

key_traits.label: Joey field observation
key_traits.text: Joey Santore's West Texas native-plant landscaping video includes an exact Clematis texensis frame showing vine habit and leaf context.
